why: The statement asks for a self-adjoint operator whose spectrum is the nontrivial zeros, which implies RH; any full claim is a landmark. Yakaboylu's v9 (simple zeros, case) and v13 (whole) are knocked down by the author's own v17 concession that self-adjointness rests on an unshown positivity equivalent to RH and that simplicity is an open question; v1 and v4 are reductions/candidates (none). The self-published or marginal RH-proof claims (Bridger, Valamontes, Tamburini, Ladjeroud, Bonelli x2, Tibedo, Aksman) each combine landmark claims, no uptake, later expert work (Connes–Consani–Moscovici, Connes 2026, Liu) still treating the problem as open, and venue/history signals, so not_credible; Tamburini was the closest call (arXiv, physics author) but the hedged conclusion and silence tipped it. Connes–Consani–Moscovici is numerical plus a self-described tentative argument with two missing steps: none. Anthropic's two-thirds proportion and OpenAI's zero-free half-plane are different questions (variant), though AI-generated by their own disclosures. Suo's operator has eigenvalues ρ(1−ρ) and non-normalizable states, a variant.
doubts: The OpenAI AI attribution rests on the repository README's general statement, not the manuscript's own disclosure. Tamburini's not_credible call is a judgement on signals; doubtful would also be defensible but leaves the outcome unchanged only if it were scoped other than whole. Yakaboylu v13 knocked_down rests on the author's own later concession rather than an outside refutation.
